english: A serpent stole the cattle of men. It had three heads. It drew them into the mountain. Then the Third One, a young warrior, grasped a spear. He climbed to the mountain and cried: Serpent, give them to me! The serpent roared, but the Third One struck its three heads. So he slew the serpent and drove them out of the mountain. Then the mountain trembled. The men gave him the first share of the herd. But the Third One said: Give it to the women; I want a name.

pie: dwóh₁ mógʰuh₁ stéh₂dʰh₁om kl̥Héni ph₂stā́m. péh₂wr̥ kʷsépi h₂én kʷḱtā́m. pr̥h₂wós prḗḱst. kʷéyes h₁énoy h₂néres? h₁éteros mléwHt. tóy bʰóres péḱu nos h₂ewsér gʷm̥yṓnti. ḱóymom dr̥mdʰí wiHróns-kʷe ǵʰuHéye. pr̥h₂wós drémt wiHrṓs-kʷe nékʷti sth₂ént. h₂éyeri h₁ludʰónt gʷréwōm widónt péḱu ne widónt. kénkont bʰugént-kʷe. nu mógʰuh₁ h₁íd spr̥tā́m. wiḱpótis tóybʰos dwóh₁ márkoh₁ h₁opéyet. nu h₁édtām suptā́m-kʷe.
english: Two young men were guarding the herd on a hill. In the night they caught sight of a fire yonder. The first asked: Who are those men yonder? The other said: They are thieves; at dawn they will come to our livestock. Run to the village and call the warriors! The first ran, and the warriors rose up in the night. In the morning they came; they found spears, they did not find livestock. They were hungry, and they fled. So the two young men rescued it. The chief gave them two horses. Then the two ate and fell asleep.

pie: h₃rḗḱs súHnum wl̥nh₁to.
english: The king wanted a son.

pie: dusménēs dʰǵʰémi ḱéyo h₁sn̥tyóḱlewēs-kʷe h₁ésmi upér sth₂éh₁yet. wéwket dusménēs. h₁sń̥tyoḱlewes me mē gʷʰéns. téwe toy gʷṓs déḱm̥-kʷe márkons déh₃oh₂. h₁sn̥tyóḱlewēs mléwHt. h₁óytom h₃m̥nh₃dʰí. nu dusménēs swóm ǵʰóstom dyḗm próti tl̥néh₂t. dyéw me ph₂ter ḱludʰí. h₁yód h₁ím dʰrugʰyṓh₂ kl̥h₂dʰí me. nu wiHróh₁ h₃m̥nh₃tā́m stéh₂dʰh₁om-kʷe néseto. dusménēs déḱm̥ márkons h₁ím h₂ewsér wédʰet h₁ím-kʷe ne dʰréwgʰt. h₁óytos sth₂éh₁yet h₂ew-kʷe ne wikétām.
english: Ill-Minded lay on the earth, and Of-True-Fame stood over him. Ill-Minded said: Of-True-Fame, do not slay me! I shall give you your cattle and ten horses. Of-True-Fame said: Swear an oath! Then Ill-Minded lifted his hand toward the sky: Father Sky, hear me! If I deceive him, strike me down! Then the two men swore, and the herd returned home. At dawn Ill-Minded led ten horses to him, and he did not deceive him. The oath stood, and the two did not fight again.

pie: tód ḱeḱluwṓs h₂ówis h₂aǵróm bʰuged.
english: Having heard this, the sheep fled into the plain.

pie: albʰós dl̥h₁gʰóḱr̥h₂nos uksḗn h₁suḱléwesey h₁ést. h₁léwdʰeyes h₁ím ǵn̥nh₃ént. h₁suḱléwēs h₁ím gʷowsth₂óy h₂éyeri ne widét. h₁ésyo lóysās h₁suh₁éḱwosyo dʰéh₁mn̥ sékʷeto. h₁súh₁eḱwe méne uksḗn téwe gʰórtoy h₁ésti. h₁suh₁éḱwos mléwHt. deywṓs moy h₁ím sl̥ǵént. h₁suḱléwēs wérh₁t. nu moy deywṓs téwe uksénm̥ sélǵonti. h₁suh₁éḱwos smḗyt h₁ésmey-kʷe dl̥h₁gʰóḱr̥h₂nom déh₃t. nu tóh₁ priHóh₁.
english: Of-Good-Fame had a white, long-horned bull. The people knew it. In the morning Of-Good-Fame did not find it in the stall. He followed its tracks to the house of Of-Good-Horses. Of-Good-Horses, my bull is in your enclosure. Of-Good-Horses said: The gods sent it to me. Of-Good-Fame said: Then the gods will send me your bull. Of-Good-Horses laughed and gave him the long-horned one. Now the two are friends.

pie: h₁ógʷʰis deywṓm gʷṓs péruni kéwdʰt. nókʷts dʰǵʰémi ḱéyo h₂éwsōs-kʷe ne gʷémt. nu wiHrós deywóǵenh₁ēs kh₂n̥ménh₁ h₁ludʰét. péruney gʷéHyet h₁íd-kʷe bʰidtó. h₁ógʷʰim gʷʰént h₁íns-kʷe úd h₂éǵet. h₁égʷʰis kréwh₂s kr̥snóm h₁ést. nu h₂éwsōs diwés dʰugh₂tḗr léwkt sóh₂wl̥-kʷe h₂wést. h₁éyes h₂éǵrons úd h₁yént dʰéǵʰōm-kʷe gʷʰért. deywṓs wiHróm gʷr̥nHént. déywoǵenh₁es téwe ḱléwos ń̥dʰgʷʰitom. h₁léwdʰeyes tód kéh₂nmn̥ h₂ewsér gʷéHyonti.
english: The serpent hid the cows of the gods in a rock. Night lay on the earth, and Dawn did not come. Then a hero, Of-Divine-Race, came with a song. He sang to the rock, and it split. He slew the serpent and drove them out. The blood of the serpent was black. Then Dawn, the daughter of Sky, shone forth, and the sun grew bright. The cows went out to the fields, and the earth grew warm. The gods praised the hero: Of-Divine-Race, your fame is imperishable! At dawn people sing that song.

pie: dwóh₁ bʰréh₂terh₁e gʷrúbʰis úd gʷh₂tā́m. pr̥h₂wós stéh₂dʰh₁om wodʰéyet h₁éteros stóygʰom péh₂st. póyḱōs stóygʰoy h₁ludʰónt ǵʰoysós-kʷe h₁éterom kélh₂t. péth₁t mért-kʷe. pr̥h₂wós h₁ésyo krépos dṓm bʰéret méh₂trey-kʷe sékʷt. gʷṓs toy bʰéroh₂ téwe suHnúm ne bʰéroh₂. méh₂tēr th₂kéh₁yet nu wéwket. gʷówes méǵʰye h₁sénti suHnús méǵʰye ne h₁ésti. nu h₁ésyo krépesi h₁épi sédt. h₁ésyeh₂s h₂énǵʰos méǵh₂ h₁ést.
english: Two brothers went out with spears. The first led the herd; the other guarded the path. Foes came on the path, and a spear struck the other. He fell and died. The first carried his body home and said to the mother: I bring you cattle, but I do not bring your son. The mother was silent, then she said: Cattle I have; a son I do not have. Then she sat down by his body. Her grief was great.

pie: h₁yód bʰṓr stéh₂dʰh₁om h₂epó h₁élh₂t snóygʷʰos h₂éǵroysu ḱéyo. stéh₂dʰh₁om pédās snóygʷʰoy linékʷt. poh₂imḗn h₁íh₂n̥s h₂ewsér kʷéḱt h₁esh₂óm-kʷe ǵʰuHéyet. h₁ésh₂e nos snóygʷʰos h₁ésyo stóygʰom déyḱeti. nu pédās déh₂nu sékʷonto gʷṓs-kʷe ssóntm̥-kʷe bʰórm̥ h₂én widétām. h₁ím sh₂imnéh₁ bʰondʰéyetām h₁íns-kʷe dʰéh₁mn̥ wodʰéyetām. snóygʷʰos bʰrṓm póyḱos. h₁esh₂ós h₁ím ne moréyet só h₁ésyo poh₂imḗn bʰúHm̥. snóygʷʰos wékʷsperoy tinéh₁t.
english: When a thief drove off the herd, snow lay on the fields. The herd left tracks in the snow. At dawn the shepherd caught sight of them and called the master: Master, the snow points out to us his path! Then the two followed the tracks to the river, and there they found the cattle and the sleeping thief. They bound him with a rope, and they led the cattle home. Snow is the foe of thieves. The master did not kill him; that one became his herdsman. In the evening the snow melted.

pie: wiHrṓs n̥sént ǵérh₂onts-kʷe h₃rḗǵs tóns prḗḱst. kʷóti gʷṓs h₂éǵete? tóti h₂éǵome h₁yóti h₂stéres dyéwi h₁sénti. h₃rḗǵs smḗyt. h₂stéres polh₁éwes yúH péh₂urōs. mē me dʰrugʰyéte. kʷóti h₂éǵete? mógʰus sékʷt. ḱm̥tóm gʷṓs déḱm̥ uksénn̥s albʰóm-kʷe h₁éḱwom h₂éǵome. h₃rḗǵs wérh₁t. téwe wékʷos h₁sónt. h₁ím moy wédʰete. mógʰus h₁ím h₃réǵm̥ wodʰéyet h₃rḗǵs-kʷe h₁ésmey h₂éh₂usom h₁opéyet.
english: The warriors came home unharmed, and the old king asked them: How many cows did you drive? We drove so many as there are stars in the sky. The king laughed: The stars are many, but you are few. Do not deceive me! How many did you drive? A young man said: We drove a hundred cows, ten bulls and a white horse. The king said: Your word is true. Lead it to me! The young man led it to the king, and the king gave him gold.

pie: h₂yuHn̥ḱṓs wĺ̥kʷōm skéwHtins wésn̥to. kl̥Hn̥sú tḱiyént h₂eh₃móm-kʷe mḗms h₁édn̥t. h₁éysōm h₃dóntes h₂eḱrṓs h₁sént. snóygʷʰos kl̥Hn̥sú dʰubʰrós h₁ést. h₁éysōm méh₂teres h₁íns ne ǵn̥nh₃ént. gʰostéyōm gʷṓs yéh₁n̥s tr̥méni ǵʰyént. swóybʰos ph₂tr̥bʰós h₁íns h₂l̥gʷʰént. ph₂téres sokʷéyont. nu yúH wiHrṓs yúH ne wĺ̥kʷōs. ḱléwos wos méǵh₂ h₁éseti. nu h₂yuHn̥ḱṓs sméyn̥t h₁éysōm-kʷe méh₂teres méwdont.
english: The young men wore the skins of wolves. They dwelt on the hills, and they ate raw meat. Their teeth were sharp. The snow on the hills was deep. Their mothers did not recognize them. At the end of the year they drove the cattle of the enemies. They brought them in to their fathers. The fathers said: Now you are men; you are not wolves. Your fame will be great. Then the young men laughed, and their mothers rejoiced.

pie: ph₂tḗr suHnówey h₂roh₁dʰéyet. méne súHnew Hyudʰsmṓys ḱóm gʷéh₂esi. gʰostéyōm gʷrúbʰos mē tréses téwe-kʷe priHóns mē linékʷs. h₁yós swóns priHóns linékʷti ḱléwos tósmey ne h₁ésti. nu h₁ésmey h₂éyesos ǵʰoysóm déh₃t. nu suHnús tṓys ḱóm h₁éyt tritéh₂i-kʷe kʷsépi nést. polh₁úns gʷṓs h₂élgʷʰt. h₁ésyo ǵʰoysós kruh₂séh₁ h₁rudʰéh₁t. méh₂tēr méwdet bʰéh₂t-kʷe. méne súHnew túH kéh₂ilos. nu téwe h₁nómn̥ ḱlutóm h₁ludʰísu h₁entér h₁éseti. pótis h₁ésyeh₂s wékʷesh₂ ḱléwt smḗyt-kʷe.
english: The father spoke to the son: My son, you will go with the warriors. Do not tremble before the spears of the enemies, and do not leave your friends. Whoever leaves his friends, to him there is no fame. Then he gave him a spear of bronze. Then the son went with them, and on the third night he came home unharmed. He brought in many cows. His spear was red with blood. The mother rejoiced and spoke: My son, you are whole! Now your name will be famous among the people. Her husband heard her words and smiled.

pie: dusménēs dʰéyǵʰesi h₁épi sth₂éh₁yet wrégontbʰos-kʷe wiHróybʰos HréwdHt. gʷówes wos méne gʰórtoy h₁sénti méne-kʷe gʰréh₁mn̥ h₁édn̥ti. gʷm̥té h₁íns-kʷe h₁áydʰwe h₁yód dʰérsete. h₁wesuḱléwēs h₁ésmey wérh₁yet. dúsmenes téwe wékʷesh₂ h₂enh₁mos. téwe h₁ésh₂r̥ wékʷsperoy dʰǵʰémi h₁rudʰéh₁eti ḱwónes-kʷe h₁íd léyǵʰonti. nu ǵʰoysóm Hyéh₁kt só-kʷe dusménesos h₁óh₃s kélh₂t. dʰéyǵʰesos péth₁t h₁ésyo-kʷe h₂néres bʰugént. h₁wesuḱléwēs dʰéyǵʰos Hrunépt h₁íns-kʷe ḱóymom h₁élh₂t.
english: Ill-Minded stood on the wall and shouted to the pursuing warriors: Your cows are in my enclosure, and they eat my grass! Come and take them, if you dare! Of-Goodly-Fame answered him: Ill-Minded, your words are wind. In the evening your blood will be red on the earth, and the dogs will lick it. Then he threw a spear, and it struck Ill-Minded in the mouth. He fell from the wall, and his men fled. Of-Goodly-Fame broke the wall and drove the cows to the village.

pie: wiHrṓs nékʷti ph₂wéni péri sédyont h₁éysōm-kʷe ḱérdh₂ mudréh₂ h₁ést. h₂yuHn̥ḱós néwom kéh₂nmn̥ gʷéHyet. pérwr̥ kʷsépi pr̥mé. gʰostéys gʷṓs ǵʰimé gʰóstis-kʷe sést. nu nos h₂mélǵos dédh₃n̥ti h₂mélǵos-kʷe sweh₂déwih₂m. wiHrṓs sméyn̥t ph₃ént-kʷe. ǵérh₂onts h₂roh₁dʰéyet. th₂kéh₁yete. h₂ṓwsih₁ gʰostéyey h₁stés. h₂yuHn̥ḱós th₂kéh₁yet wiHrṓs-kʷe l̥gʰént. h₂stéres luként.
english: At night the warriors sat around the fire, and their hearts were glad. A young man sang a new song: In the night we crossed the ford. We drove the cows of the enemy, and the enemy slept. Now they give us milk, and the milk is sweet. The warriors laughed and drank. But an old man spoke: Be silent! The enemy has ears. The young man was silent, and the warriors lay down. The stars grew bright.

pie: deywóḱlewesos h₁éḱwōm gʷriHwéh₂es dl̥h₁gʰéh₂es h₁sént. deywóḱlewēs tóybʰos h₂roh₁dʰéyet. HéHḱuh₁ me h₁éḱwoh₁ gʰostéyōm gʰórtons bʰéretom gʷíh₃wontm̥-kʷe h₁mé ḱóymom wédʰetom. h₁yód méroh₂ ḱwn̥bʰós méne krépos mē linkʷih₁tóm. nu Hróth₂oy stéh₂t. nu h₁éḱwoh₁ swóns ḱérh₂sonn̥s nutā́m gʰóstins-kʷe próti tékʷetām. gʷíh₃wontm̥ h₁ím ḱóymom wékʷsperoy bʰéretām tóybʰos-kʷe wódr̥ gʰréh₁mn̥-kʷe h₁opéyet.
english: The manes of the two horses of Fame-from-the-Gods were long. He spoke to them: Swift horses, carry me to the enclosures of the enemies, and lead me back to the village alive. If I die, may you not leave my body to the dogs. Then he stood up in the chariot. Then the horses bowed their heads and ran toward the enemies. In the evening they carried him back alive to the village, and he gave them water and grass.

pie: h₂yuHn̥ḱṓs Hyudʰsmṓys ph₂wéni péri sédyont. péh₂wr̥ gʷʰréh₁yet. ǵérh₂onts tóybʰos wéwket. mógʰewes méne wékʷesh₂ ḱluté. gʷówes m̥rént ǵn̥h₁yóm mért ḱléwos ne mért. h₁uséws wiHrósyo ḱléwos ń̥dʰgʷʰitom. gʰostéys péḱu mē klépete. h₁yós gʰóstim dʰrugʰyéti deywṓs tóm dedr̥ḱḗr. póyḱōm márkons h₂éǵete bʰoh₂góns-kʷe wos ḱóymom bʰérete. ḱl̥nwént h₁ésyo-kʷe wékʷesh₂ h₁éysōm ḱr̥dsú dʰédʰh₁n̥t. polh₁úns márkons pós h₂l̥gʷʰént ǵr̥h₂n̥téy-kʷe h₁wésum bʰoh₂góm dh₃ént.
english: The young warriors were sitting around the fire. The fire was warm. An old man said to them: Young men, hear my words. Cattle die, kin die, but fame does not die. The fame of a good man is imperishable. Do not steal the livestock of a guest. Whoever deceives a guest, the gods see him. Drive the horses of the foes, and carry your shares to the village! They listened, and they placed his words in their hearts. Afterwards they brought in many horses, and they gave the old man a good share.

pie: h₁suǵénh₁ēs dusḱléwesos stégos h₁r̥sḱét sékʷt-kʷe. téwe h₂néres méne bʰréh₂term̥ gʷʰnént. ḱm̥tóm moy gʷṓs h₁íh₁ h₂m̥bʰí dh₃dʰí gʷrúbʰis-wē gʷm̥yṓmes. dusḱléwēs wéwket. ne toy kʷid dʰl̥gʰóh₂. téwe bʰréh₂tēr bʰṓr méne h₂éǵrom wéyḱt. méne péḱu stéh₂yet mért-kʷe. h₁suǵénh₁ēs h₂roh₁dʰéyet. nu deywṓs h₁sónt widéh₁yōnti. swéh₂m tewtéh₂m léytt dusḱléwēs-kʷe ḱérdi trémt. h₁ésyo tewtéh₂ ḱm̥tóm h₂ówins h₁suǵénh₁esos stégos h₂éyeri wédʰet. h₁suǵénh₁ēs h₁íh₂n̥s h₁áyto gʷrúbʰis-kʷe h₂ew ne gʷémt. ǵn̥h₃rós wiHrós h₂ówins h₁áyto h₁ésh₂r̥ ne h₁áyto.
english: Of-Good-Race came to the house of Ill-Famed and said: Your men slew my brother. Give me a hundred cattle in exchange for him, or we shall come with spears. Ill-Famed answered: I owe you nothing. Your brother, a thief, entered my field. He stole my livestock, and he died. Of-Good-Race spoke: Then the gods will see the truth. He went away to his own people, and Ill-Famed trembled in his heart. In the morning his people led a hundred sheep to the house of Of-Good-Race. Of-Good-Race took them, and he did not come again with spears. A wise man takes sheep; he does not take blood.

pie: wiHrṓs gʰostéys pḱúh₁ ḱóm n̥sént. gʷénh₂es téḱneh₂-kʷe dʰh₁mń̥bʰos h₁éǵʰs gʷm̥yónt. h₁suḱléwesos pótnih₂ swóm pótim kʷéḱt prḗḱst-kʷe. kúdʰe méne bʰréh₂tēr h₁ésti? pótis wérh₁yet. só pr̥wéni ḱéyor h₁ésyo ḱléwos gʷíh₃weti. nu ugʷsénm̥ moréyont mḗms-kʷe kʷéroy pékʷont. téḱneh₂ mḗms h₁ḗdt lóyget-kʷe. h₂énHos bʰréh₂tr̥s spélom séngʷʰet. pótnih₂ ph₂wéni h₁épi sédt th₂kéh₁yet-kʷe. mḗms sweh₂dú h₁ést médʰu-kʷe tewh₂sóm h₁ést.
english: The warriors came home unharmed with the livestock of the enemy. The women and the children came out of the houses. The wife of Of-Good-Fame caught sight of her husband and asked: Where is my brother? The husband said: He lies at the ford, but his fame lives. Then they killed an ox and cooked the meat in a cauldron. The children ate meat and played. The grandmother sang the story of the brother. The wife sat down by the fire and was silent. The meat was sweet, and the mead was strong.

pie: HeHḱuh₁éḱwos m̥dʰéws péh₃tlom déh₂newi h₁épi dʰéh₁t deywóns-kʷe ǵʰuHéyet. déywōs me h₁uséwōm déh₃tores ḱluté. gʰostéys moy gʷṓs dh₃té pr̥h₂wóm-kʷe wos uksénm̥ déh₃oh₂. méne h₁éḱwōs HeHḱéwes h₁sih₁ént méne-kʷe gʷéru mē Hrumpih₁tó. nu déh₂nu h₂nr̥bʰís ḱóm térh₂t. h₂ewsér ḱm̥tóm ugʷsn̥bʰís ḱóm nést deywóybʰos-kʷe uksénm̥ déh₃t. h₁ésyo wiHrṓs h₁ím gʷr̥nHént h₁íns-kʷe bʰéh₂gont.
english: Of-Swift-Horses set a cup of mead by the river and called upon the gods: Gods, givers of good things, hear me! Give me the cattle of the enemy, and I shall give you the first bull. May my horses be swift, and may my spear not break! Then with men he crossed over the river. At dawn he came home unharmed with a hundred oxen, and he gave the bull to the gods. His men praised him, and they divided the oxen.

pie: wiHrṓs gʷṓs wiḱpóteys dʰh₁méni bʰéh₂gont. wiḱpótis pr̥h₂wóm bʰoh₂góm h₁áyto mogʰúbʰos-kʷe uksénn̥s déh₃t. h₁yós gʰórtom péh₂st tósmey dwóyh₁ h₂ówih₁ dh₃ént. nu mógʰewes h₁ím gʷr̥nHént. h₁uséwōm déh₃tor téwe ḱléwos ń̥dʰgʷʰitom h₁syéh₁t. mléwHt. gʷówes h₂n̥rṓm ḱléwos. h₁yós h₁íns gʰostéys h₂éǵeti só bʰoh₂góm bʰgih₁tó. mḗms nékʷti h₁édn̥t médʰu-kʷe ph₃ént ǵérh₂onts-kʷe kéh₂nmn̥ kh₂nét. ḱwónes kʷérom liǵʰént. nu swépnos mógʰuns gʷémt péh₂wr̥-kʷe stéwdt.
english: In the house of the clan chief the warriors divided the cattle. The chief took the first share, and he gave bulls to the young men. He who had guarded the enclosure, to him they gave two sheep. Then the young men praised him: Giver of good things, may your fame be imperishable! He said: Cattle are the fame of men. Whoever drives them from the enemy, may he receive his share. In the night they ate meat and drank mead, and an old man chanted a song. The dogs licked the cauldron. Then sleep came to the young men, and the fire grew cold.

pie: h₁suménēs deywóḱlewesos dʰugh₂térm̥ h₁épt deywóḱlewēs-kʷe h₁suménesos suHnúbʰos lémbʰt. dwóh₁ ph₂térh₁e pr̥wéni ǵn̥h₃n̥tó. h₂roh₁dʰéyet h₁suménēs. méne moy suHnúm dh₃dʰí téwe-kʷe toy dʰugh₂térm̥ déh₃oh₂. deywóḱlewēs wérh₁yet. téwe suHnús ḱuh₁rós méne-kʷe dʰugh₂tḗr péh₂ureh₂ déḱm̥ moy h₂ówins éti dh₃dʰí. h₁suménēs sokʷéyet. h₂ówim toy ne déh₃oh₂. nu deywóḱlewēs smḗyt ph₂térh₁e-kʷe swéh₂ téḱneh₂ mith₂tā́m. kʷyéh₁tis pr̥wéni h₁ést. dʰugh₂tḗr dʰéh₁mn̥ drémt.
english: Kindly had seized the daughter of Fame-from-the-Gods, and Fame-from-the-Gods had seized the son of Kindly. The two fathers met at the ford. Kindly spoke: Give me my son, and I shall give you your daughter. Fame-from-the-Gods said: Your son is strong, and my daughter is small; give me ten sheep besides. Kindly said: I shall not give you a sheep. Then Fame-from-the-Gods laughed, and the two fathers exchanged their children. Then there was quiet at the ford. The daughter ran home.

pie: h₂yéwHō poh₂imḗn gʰóstipoteys dṓm h₂ewsér drémt. gʰóstipotey bʰóres nékʷti h₁ludʰónt péḱu-kʷe nos h₂epó h₂éǵont. bʰéwgm̥ twé-kʷe h₁érm̥. gʰóstipotis prḗḱst. kʷéyes bʰóres? kúdʰe h₁íd duként? poh₂imḗn bʰéh₂t. tóy dusḱléwesos h₂néres h₁sént h₁íd bʰérǵʰons próti duként. nu gʰóstipotis gʷéru kapyét ǵn̥h₁yóm-kʷe ǵʰuHéyet. h₁íns HeHḱúbʰis h₁éḱwōys wrégōmes. ǵn̥h₁yóm márkons yéwgt poh₂imḗn-kʷe h₁éymos stóygʰom déyḱet. stóygʰom énu tékʷont ḱwónes-kʷe pró tékʷont. h₁éysōm gʷéruh₂ sh₂wéni léh₂pt. kr̥snéh₂es h₂éweyes stóygʰoy upér HrudHént.
english: At dawn a young herdsman ran to the house of the lord. Lord, thieves came in the night, and they drove off our livestock. I fled and came to you. The lord asked: Who are the thieves? Where did they lead it? The herdsman spoke: They were men of Ill-Famed; they led it toward the hills. Then the lord grasped a spear and called the kin: Let us pursue them with swift horses! The kin yoked horses, and the herdsman showed them the path. They ran along the path, and the dogs ran before them. Their spears flashed in the sun. Black birds cried over the path.

pie: dwóh₁ wiHróh₁ albʰóm uksénm̥ uḱtā́m. pr̥h₂wós wéwket. h₁eǵóh₂ gʰostéys gʰórtoy pr̥h₂wós h₁ésm̥. h₁éteros sokʷéyet. h₁eǵóh₂ h₁ím méne ǵʰóstoh₁ h₂epó wédʰom. nu gʰóstipotis tóybʰos h₂roh₁dʰéyet. uksḗn swóm pótim wl̥h₁yéh₁t. h₁ím wiHróysu h₁entér dʰéh₁t. h₁éteros h₁ésmey wódr̥ déh₃t. nu uksḗn tóm gʷéh₂t pr̥h₂wós-kʷe th₂kéh₁yet. wiHrṓs wérh₁yonti. ugʷsḗn tóm ǵn̥néh₃ti h₁yós h₁ésmey wódr̥ dédeh₃ti.
english: Two warriors wanted a white bull. The first said: I was the first in the enclosure of the enemy. The other said: But I led it away with my hand. Then the lord spoke to the two: May the bull choose its own master. He set it between the two warriors. The other had given it water. Then the bull went to him, and the first was silent. The warriors say: An ox knows the one who gives it water.

pie: Hyudʰsmós polh₁úns ugʷsénn̥s h₂éǵontm̥ poh₂iménm̥ stóygʰoy ǵnéh₃t. stóygʰos dweh₂rós h₁ést. kʷís ḱóysōm ugʷsnṓm pótis? poh₂imḗn wérh₁yet. h₁éysōm pótis ḱósyeh₂s tewtéh₂s h₃rḗǵs. kúdʰe h₁íns h₂éǵesi? h₁íns déh₂nu h₂éǵoh₂ tr̥syónti. Hyudʰsmós wéwket. déḱm̥ moy ugʷsénn̥s dh₃dʰí gʷéh₂esi-kʷe. poh₂imḗn sokʷéyet. h₃rēǵés wiHrṓs stóygʰoy gʷm̥sḱónti. nu Hyudʰsmós tóns kʷéḱt léytt-kʷe. poh₂imḗn smḗyt h₁íns-kʷe wódr̥ wodʰéyet.
english: On the road a warrior met a herdsman driving many oxen. The road was long. Who is the master of these oxen? The herdsman said: Their master is the king of this people. Where are you driving them? I am driving them to the river; they are thirsty. The warrior said: Give me ten oxen, and you will go. The herdsman answered: The warriors of the king are coming on the road. Then the warrior caught sight of them and went away. The herdsman laughed and led the oxen to the water.

pie: gʰóstis h₁wesuḱléwesos dṓm h₁ludʰét. h₁wesuḱléwēs h₁ésmey mḗms médʰu-kʷe déh₃t. gʰóstis h₁ḗdt péh₃t-kʷe. sést nékʷti stéh₂t albʰóm-kʷe gʷṓm h₂epó h₁élh₂t. h₁esh₂ós h₁ím h₂éyeri sékʷeto h₁ím-kʷe déh₂newi widét. kʷíd me gʰóstey dʰréwgʰs? mḗms toy médʰu-kʷe déh₃m̥. gʰóstis mléwHt. h₁eǵóh₂ ne téwe gʰóstis h₁eǵóh₂ téwe póyḱos. nu h₂én wikétām h₁wesuḱléwēs-kʷe gʰóstim gʷʰént. h₁ésyo krépos h₂én ḱéyo. h₁éy néseto. nu h₁esh₂ós gʰostíbʰos ne bʰebʰóydʰe.
english: A stranger came to the house of Of-Goodly-Fame. Of-Goodly-Fame gave him meat and mead. The stranger ate and drank. He slept, but in the night he rose up and drove off the white cow. In the morning the master followed him and found him at the river. Guest, why did you deceive me? I gave you meat and mead. The stranger said: I am not your guest; I am your foe. Then the two fought there, and Of-Goodly-Fame slew the stranger. His body lay there. The cow returned home. Now the master does not trust strangers.

pie: h₁wesuḱléwesos Hyudʰsmṓs stéh₂dʰh₁osyo lóysās sékʷonto. h₂éǵrons pér tékʷont. kónHim wékʷsperoy bʰérǵʰoy kʷḱént. nu h₂roh₁dʰéyet h₁wesuḱléwēs. príHōs bʰóres péh₂urōs wéy-kʷe polh₁éwes. h₁éymos mē bʰebʰéyh₂omes. nu bʰérǵʰom stéygʰont póyḱōs-kʷe bʰugént. péh₂wr̥ h₂én dʰh₁ént mḗms-kʷe pékʷont. nu stéh₂dʰh₁om ḱóymom h₁l̥h₂ént mudént-kʷe. h₁wesuḱléwēs HréwdHt. ne kʷid lelóykʷe. h₁ésyo priHṓs sméyn̥t h₁ím-kʷe gʷr̥nHént. tósyeh₂i nékʷti h₂str̥sú Hn̥dʰí ssént.
english: The warriors of Of-Goodly-Fame followed the tracks of the herd. Through the fields they ran. In the evening they caught sight of dust on a hill. Then Of-Goodly-Fame spoke: Friends, the thieves are few, and we are many. Let us not fear them! Then they climbed the hill, and the foes fled. There they set a fire and cooked meat. Then they drove the herd to the village and rejoiced. Of-Goodly-Fame cried: Nothing is missing! His friends laughed and praised him. That night they slept under the stars.

pie: eḱwōs tu ewewkʷont, "ḱludʰi, owei, ḱēr gʰe agʰnutoi n̥smei widn̥tbʰ(y)os (widn̥tmos): nēr, potis, owiōm r̥ wl̥Hnām sebʰi gʷʰermom westrom kʷrn̥euti. neǵʰi owiōm wl̥Hnā esti."
english: The horses said: "Listen, sheep, our hearts pain us when we see this: a man, the master, makes the wool of the sheep into a warm garment for himself. And the sheep has no wool."

pie: méǵh₂s ḱwṓ ǵr̥h₂n̥tés péḱu péh₂st. tréyes gʰósteyes dʰéyǵʰos nékʷti tr̥h₂ént. ḱwṓ stéh₂t pr̥h₂wóm-kʷe h₁épt. gʰósteyes HrudHént ǵérh₂onts-kʷe bʰéwdʰt. gʷéru lémbʰt stégesos-kʷe h₁éǵʰs gʷémt. tóybʰos mléwHt. gʰósteyes bʰugté. deywṓs méne péḱu h₂léksonti. gʰósteyes kʷsépm̥ h₁n̥dó bʰugént ḱwṓ-kʷe gʷowsth₂óy ḱóm h₂ew légʰt. ǵérh₂onts h₁ésmey mḗms déh₃t. h₁íd h₁ḗdt swépt-kʷe. nu ḱunéy sékʷt. ḱwón túH tewh₂sós. ǵérh₂onts tríns ǵʰoysóns h₂éyeri dʰéyǵʰesi h₁épi widét.
english: A great dog guarded the livestock of an old man. In the night three strangers crossed over the wall. The dog rose up and seized the first one. The strangers cried out, and the old man woke. He seized a spear and stepped out of the house. He said to them: Flee, strangers! The gods guard my livestock. The strangers fled into the night, and the dog lay down again beside the stall. The old man gave it meat. It ate it and fell asleep. Then he said to the dog: Dog, you are strong. In the morning the old man found three spears by the wall.
